extracted.intended_audience: peer reviewers for IgMin Research (Biology, Medicine, and Engineering)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for external peer reviewers assessing manuscripts submitted to IgMin Research (a multidisciplinary open-access journal in Biology, Medicine, and Engineering), covering expectations for objectivity, timeliness, confidentiality, ethics, feedback quality, citations, revisions, and respect for authorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective Review
rubrics_metrics.description: Commitment to an objective and unbiased evaluation of submitted manuscripts; assess research on scientific merit rather than personal biases or preferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess validity, methodology, interpretation, and significance; be vigilant against affiliations, relationships, or beliefs that could bias judgment and recuse if conflicts exist; distinguish constructive criticism from subjective preferences; provide rigorous, evidence-based evaluation; consider broader impact, relevance to current debates, alignment with existing theories; provide specific feedback to identify methodological flaws, inconsistencies in interpretation, or literature gaps; channel expert perspective into balanced assessments that advance knowledge and intellectual integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timely Response
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide reviews within recommended timelines to support efficient publication and the research ecosystem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended timelines (from date of assignment): short articles (up to 5 pages, basic methodology) — 2 days; regular research articles (6–15 pages, moderate complexity) — 3 days; complex research articles (16+ pages, specialized methodologies) — 5 days; special issues/thematic articles — follow above by individual article, editorial team may allow up to 7 days. If unable to meet deadlines, communicate promptly with editors to allow adjustments. Balance comprehensiveness with promptness; editors set reasonable timelines and offer acknowledgments/certificates/incentives for timely reviews. Honor commitments where possible; notify editorial team early about availability/conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain strict confidentiality of manuscript contents and identities under the journal's double-blind peer review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not discuss or share the manuscript, its findings, or its existence with anyone not directly involved in the review; uphold anonymity of authors and reviewers; safeguard proprietary aspects and any insights that could affect your own work; report suspected breaches (public sharing, plagiarism, mishandling) to the editorial team; understand that breaching confidentiality can damage trust, reputation, and may have legal consequences; use journal-provided secure platforms for communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive Feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide insightful, actionable, balanced feedback that helps authors improve their manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make feedback clear and specific, pointing to sections/figures/arguments that need attention; balance strengths and weaknesses; support critiques with evidence from the manuscript or literature; prioritize key issues with the most impact (research question clarity, methodology appropriateness, data interpretation, scope alignment); suggest practical solutions or alternatives rather than only pointing out problems; maintain professional, respectful tone, avoiding personal comments and overly negative language; ensure comments are confidential and impartial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical Considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Vigilance for ethical issues including plagiarism, data manipulation/fabrication, appropriate authorship, ethical review/consent, conflicts of interest, and duplicate submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be alert for plagiarism and use detection tools where appropriate; check for signs of data manipulation or fabrication (inconsistencies, suspiciously perfect patterns) and report concerns to editors; verify authorship lists and alignment of contributions with affiliations, flag misrepresentation or omissions; for studies with human/animal subjects check for statements of ethical approval and informed consent; ensure conflicts of interest are disclosed; watch for dual submission/duplicate publication and notify editors if suspected; your scrutiny helps uphold research integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear Communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliver well-structured, informative reviews using clear language to guide authors and editors effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin with a concise summary of main findings and contributions; structure comments logically (e.g., by manuscript sections: introduction, methods, results, discussion); use specific examples from the manuscript; provide in-text comments for precise locations and a summative overall assessment; break down complex concepts into simpler terms for cross-disciplinary readers; maintain balanced tone; be prepared to respond courteously to author queries and engage in constructive dialogue; when evaluating revisions, acknowledge addressed items and indicate remaining issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of Conflicts of Interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Declare any professional, financial, or personal interests that could influence objectivity; recognize that perceived conflicts also matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify types of conflicts: financial ties (consultancies, investments), personal/professional relationships (collaborators, mentors), competing research agendas, and strong personal beliefs; disclose potential conflicts promptly to editors and recuse from review if impartiality is compromised; transparency protects authors, readers, and the journal's reputation; disclosure is a commitment to ethical conduct rather than a stigma.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation and References
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the accuracy, relevance, completeness, and ethical use of citations and references supporting manuscript claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that every claim is supported by appropriate, verifiable references; assess currency and relevance of cited literature (include recent advances as well as foundational works); verify completeness — look for missing seminal works or important related studies; ensure consistent citation style and adequate bibliographic details for locating sources; encourage primary sources over secondary reviews when possible; evaluate contextualization of cited works and whether claims accurately reflect sources; watch for excessive self-citation and balance of external references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision Assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess revised manuscripts to ensure authors have effectively addressed reviewers' and editors' concerns and that the manuscript meets publication standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revisit original comments and verify that authors have responded adequately to each concern; evaluate improvements in clarity, structure, and presentation; scrutinize any methodological or analytical changes for appropriateness and robustness; check whether ethical issues previously raised have been resolved; assess authors' responses to specific comments for sufficiency and scientific rationale; evaluate contribution to the field after revisions and any added experiments or analyses for significance; judge overall suitability for publication and continue to provide constructive guidance where gaps remain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect for Authorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Approach reviews with respect, empathy, and professionalism, recognizing authors' effort and promoting collaborative improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice mutual understanding: acknowledge the time and effort behind manuscripts; frame critique constructively to guide improvement rather than disparage; be sensitive to cultural and linguistic diversity—avoid biased or dismissive language; balance rigorous critique with empathy, appreciating authors' constraints; foster collegial dialogue that encourages revisions and collaboration; respectful reviews increase likelihood of constructive engagement and strengthen the scholarly community.
